cohort: The study included 324 pregnancy-associated hospitalizations and 3,805 nonpregnancy-associated hospitalizations for reproductive-aged female patients who received ECMO therapy, identified from the 2013 to 2019 National Readmissions Database.
finding: Pregnancy-associated ECMO therapy was associated with a lower incidence of in-hospital death, bleeding complications, shorter length of stay, and lower total hospital costs compared to nonpregnancy-associated ECMO therapy, without an increased risk of thromboembolic complications.
